findings.title: Flex layout disables the action button's right float
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so its direct `button` child is a flex item. Per the flexbox layout rules, the existing `float: right` on that item computes to `none`; without `margin-left: auto`, `justify-content`, or another positioning rule, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge. This regresses the placement of small-action controls and can push them off the row when the description is wide. Add an explicit flex alignment rule (for example `margin-left: auto` on the button, with appropriate shrinking/growth for the description).

findings.title: The flex alignment mixin omits the Mozilla legacy box property
findings.body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` deliberately emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box`, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. Firefox versions using the legacy box implementation will therefore ignore every `@include align-items(...)` call and use the legacy default alignment (stretch), including the newly centered header contents and baseline-aligned bullet badges. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside the other legacy declarations, or remove the unsupported legacy display mode if that browser family is no longer supported.
